transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for having me. Um... I really hope I'm not wasting your time today. It's, well, it's a little embarrassing to even bring up, to be honest. I'm a construction worker, you know, so I shouldn't really care about this kind of stuff, but... I just can't stop seeing this... this rough, kind of sunken-looking patch on my face. 

Every time I walk past a mirror or see a picture of myself, it's all I can focus on. It just makes one whole side of me look really old and beat-up. My family and people I know, they keep saying they barely notice anything at all, which is a relief, I guess, but... I just can't get it out of my head. I hope I'm explaining that okay. Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Have you noticed any changes in your skin, like a rash, dryness, or irritation, in the area you're concerned about?

No, no, nothing like that. It's not itchy or red, or peeling... nothing you'd need a cream for, I don't think. It's just the shape of it, the way it looks. I mean, I'm out in the sun and dirt all day, so my skin's not exactly perfect anyway, you know? But it's not a medical skin condition, if that makes sense. Does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Can you describe exactly what you see in the mirror that bothers you? Do you think it looks worse than it actually is, or do you feel like it’s a flaw that others must notice even if they don’t say anything?

Well, um... I guess, like I was saying before, it's just this... this patch right here. It just looks really rough and sunken in. Whenever I look in the mirror, or if my wife snaps a photo of me, it's the only thing I can see. It just makes that whole side of my face look so old and beat-up. I know I already said that, sorry to repeat myself. 

But to answer your question about whether it's worse than it actually is... gosh, I don't know. My family, they swear they barely notice anything at all. So maybe I am just making a mountain out of a molehill? I really don't want to sound vain or obsessed with my looks, especially at my age and in my line of work. But... I just feel like people *have* to see it, you know? Like maybe they're just being polite and not saying anything so they don't hurt my feelings. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way. I just don't want you to think I'm crazy for bringing it up.

latest_inference.note: The patient's preoccupation with a perceived physical flaw (specifically facial asymmetry or appearance), despite reassurance from others and no objective medical abnormality, is consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22). F45.8 (Other somatic symptom disorders) is ruled out as the presentation is more specific to body image concerns rather than general somatic symptoms.
